blocks.text: The Secret of Success and Happiness

inline.s: (Excerpt from Eckhart Tolle’s A New Earth)
The secret of success and happiness:
Being one with life, which means being one with the present moment.
As your thoughts and emotions arise,
become aware of them.
All of these are assumptions — thoughts that are unexamined and confused with reality. They are stories the ego fabricates to make you believe that you cannot be at peace right now
or that you cannot fully be yourself. Being at peace and being yourself

are one and the same thing. The ego says: Perhaps at some point in the future, if certain things happen, or other things come about, or if I can get this or become that, then I will be able to be at peace. Or it may say: Because of things that happened in the past, I can never be at peace. You can listen to everyone’s stories and discover that they could all bear the same title: “Why I cannot be at peace right now
The ego does not know that the only opportunity you have to be at peace
is now. Or perhaps it does know, but it is afraid you will discover this fact. After all, peace is the end of the ego.

How can you be at peace right now? Make peace with the present moment. The present moment is the field on which the game of life is played; it cannot be played anywhere else. Once you have made peace with the present moment, see what happens next, what you can do or choose to do, or rather what life does through you.
A few words can express the secret of the art of living, and the secret of all success and happiness: be one with life. Being one with life is being one with the present moment.
Then you will come to understand that it is not really you who lives your life, but life that lives itself through you. Life is the dancer, and you are the dance.

The ego loves its resentment of reality. And what is reality? Reality is what is (what ever is) — whatever it may be. The Buddha called it “tatata” — the suchness of life — and it is simply the suchness of this present moment. Resistance to suchness is one of the ego’s most important features. It creates the negative states in which the ego thrives

and the unhappiness it loves. In doing so, you make yourself and others suffer without knowing it, unaware that you are creating hell on earth. The essence of unconscious living is this: to create suffering without realizing it — to be entirely in the grip of the ego.

The ego’s ability to recognize itself and its own doings is astonishingly, unbelievably poor. It will condemn other people’s behavior while remaining utterly blind to the fact that it is doing the very same thing. When others point it out, it distorts the facts with angry denial, sophistry, and self-justification. Not only do individuals do this — organizations and even governments do as well. When none of these work, the ego resorts in fury to abuse, even to violent behavior — to force at the slightest provocation. Now we can understand
the words of profound wisdom Jesus spoke on the cross: “Forgive them, for they know not what they do.”

If you wish to end the misery that has weighed upon the human condition for thousands of years, you must begin with yourself, taking responsibility for your inner state at every moment. And every moment means now. Ask yourself: “Is there any negativity in me at this moment?” Then remain alert, attending to your thoughts and emotions. Notice those lesser degrees of unhappiness, in whatever forms I described earlier, such as discontent, nervous tension, being “fed up,” and so on. Notice the thoughts that try to justify or explain these unhappy emotions — for they are the very cause of the unhappiness. The moment you become aware of a negative state within you, it does not mean you have failed; it means you have succeeded!

Before awareness arises, you are identified with your inner states — your thoughts, emotions, and reactions — and this identification is the ego. When awareness comes, you are freed from identification with thoughts, emotions, and reactions. Do not confuse this with denial. You can perceive thoughts, emotions, and reactions, and the moment you feel them, freedom from identification happens naturally. Your sense of self, and of who you are, is transformed. Before, you were your thoughts, emotions, and reactions; now you are that awareness — the conscious presence that witnesses these states.
“One day I will be free of the ego.” Who is saying that? The ego, of course. Being free of the ego is actually no great feat; it is a very small thing. All you need to do is:
become aware of your thoughts and emotions as they arise.

This is not something to “do”; it is simply alert watching. In this sense, there is nothing you can “do” to free yourself of the ego. When the shift happens — the shift from thinking to awareness — an intelligence far greater than the ego’s cleverness

begins to operate in your life. Through awareness, emotions — even thoughts — are no longer personal. Their impersonal nature reveals itself naturally. Among them there is no longer an “I.” They are simply human emotions, human thoughts. Your entire personal history turns out, in the end, to be no more than a story, a collection of thoughts and emotions! They become secondary and no longer occupy the foreground of your consciousness. They no longer form the basis of your sense of self. You are the light of presence — an awareness deeper than any thought or emotion, one that exists before them.
